info.title: Drupflare Dashboard API
info.description: The HTTP API behind the Drupflare dashboard. Every operation names the permission it checks in x-action and its rate class in x-rate-class.

get.description: Cloudflare credit balance, billable usage by service, account headroom, and the work in flight. The Cloudflare reads are cached for 60 seconds. Needs the admin role and a Cloudflare Access login.
The newest operations first across every shard: type, status, verification and, for a failed one, the plain reason it stopped.
The newest organizations first across every shard.
Counts of users, organisations, sites by state and operations by status. Needs the admin role and a Cloudflare Access login.
The newest sites first across every shard. Metadata only, never site content.
The newest users first: address, name, platform role and when they joined. Never a credential or a session.

post.description: Sends a six-digit code to the address. A new address creates an account when the code is verified. The same answer comes back for every address.
Signs in with the code and sets the session cookie. The body never carries the session token.
Ends the session named by the cookie and clears it. A missing session still succeeds.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

get.summary: List the provider sign-ins that are set up
get.description: Names the providers whose client id and secret are both configured, so the sign-in screen shows only buttons that can work.

Checks the state against the cookie, exchanges the code and signs in. A provider email that matches an existing account never signs in or merges: the answer is link_required, and the person confirms the link from that account in settings.

Returns the provider address to send the browser to, and sets a short-lived cookie that ties the callback to this browser. The request carries state and a PKCE challenge, and asks for name and email only.

post.description: Returns the options to pass to navigator.credentials.get. The challenge works once and expires after five minutes.
Verifies the signed challenge and sets the session cookie. Every failure answers the same way.
Takes a fresh sign-in code for the signed-in address, marks the session as recently authenticated and rotates the session cookie.
Opens a hosted checkout for a managed plan. Needs a signed-in session and refuses API keys. Plans whose price has not been reviewed answer 404.
Opens the hosted portal where the organisation changes its card, reads invoices or cancels. Needs a signed-in session and refuses API keys.

get.description: Lists the plans. A price appears only after it has been reviewed, and platform administrators see every price.
Returns the account behind the session or, for an API key, the account that issued it.
Lists the provider identities linked to your account. The email code is always available and is not listed.

delete.description: Removes a linked provider identity. It needs a fresh authentication and refuses to remove your last sign-in method.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

get.description: Checks the state against the cookie and against this session, exchanges the code and connects the provider account to the signed-in account. It needs a fresh authentication. A provider account that is already connected, here or to another account, is a conflict.

post.description: Returns the provider address to send the browser to, and sets a short-lived cookie that ties the callback to this browser. The state records who started it, so only this session can finish the connection. It needs a fresh authentication.
Links the provider identity from the last provider sign-in in this browser to your account. It needs a fresh authentication, and the provider email must match your account email.

get.description: Lists the organisations you belong to, the personal organisation first and then by name. A key lists the organisations of the person who issued it, and only when its scopes allow account.read.
Lists your registered passkeys, newest first. Keys and counters are never returned.

patch.description: Changes the label of one of your passkeys. It does not need a fresh authentication.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

delete.description: Removes one of your passkeys. It needs a fresh authentication and refuses to remove your last sign-in method.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

post.description: Two calls, both needing a fresh authentication. Phase options returns the creation options. Phase verify checks the new credential against that challenge and stores it.

get.description: Lists the signed-in devices, newest first. A person holds only a handful of sessions, so the list is never paged.

delete.description: Ends every session except the one making this request. It needs a fresh authentication.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

delete.description: Ends one of your sessions. Revoking another session needs a fresh authentication. Revoking the session you are using needs none and also clears its cookie.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

get.description: Reads what the organisation in the path may do on its current plan. A null limit is unknown or negotiated and counts as no allowance. Only an activated subscription changes the plan; every other account reads as the free plan. billingAccount is true when the organisation has a Stripe customer, so the billing portal can open for it.
Returns one operation of the organisation in the path, with its steps in the order the steps run.

post.description: Starts the same work again as a new operation that carries the failed one in retryOf, and returns it. The request has no body. Only an operation that failed can be retried, and only for site creates, site updates, backups, restores and cleanups; any other type answers 422 with a plain reason. A failed create cleans up its earlier attempt first and then creates the site again under the same name. The caller needs the permission the operation was first started with. A retry that is already running or has succeeded is returned instead of starting another. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

post.summary: Check what a Cloudflare token can do
post.description: Reads what the token can see and do on the account it names. Nothing is stored and the token is not returned. It needs a signed-in session, so an API key is refused.

get.description: Lists the sites of the organisation in the path in id order. Sites still being created are left out; read their operation instead.

post.description: Starts a site create in the organisation in the path and returns its operation. The site ID is the operation target. The site is listed once its create finishes. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

Starts the move of the self-managed site in the path to a new managed site and returns its operation. The engine copies the site's database, creates the managed site on a Drupflare address, restores the copy into it and checks that it answers. The source site is never changed or deleted, and the managed copy is one-way. A database above the restore limit stops the operation with a plain reason before anything is created. The request has no body and needs a signed-in session with a recent step-up. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation. Answers 409 when the site was already adopted or another change to it is running, 422 when the site is not self-managed or not live, and 403 when the plan has no room for another site.

get.summary: List the backups of a site
get.description: Lists the backups of the site in the path, newest first. A backup too large for a restore says why and can still be exported.

post.description: Starts a backup of the site in the path and returns its operation. The dump is stored without secrets. A backup reads verified false until a scratch restore has proved it. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

get.description: Streams the backup as one SQL file. It needs a signed-in session, so an API key is refused. The dump carries no secrets. A backup of another organisation is not found. An audit row is written before the download starts.

post.summary: Restore a backup into a site
post.description: Starts a restore of the backup in the path into another site of the same organisation, or the same site, and returns its operation. The restore replaces the target database. A backup that is too large for a restore is refused. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

post.summary: Clean up a site that failed to create
post.description: Removes what a failed create left behind for the site in the path and returns the cleanup operation, whose type is repair.run. The site must never have become active; a live site answers 409. It also answers 409 while another change to the site is running. The operation stops the site serving, deletes its script, routes and resources, frees its name and marks the site deleted. A repeat on a site that is already clean returns the operation that cleaned it. The request has no body. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

Starts the delete of the site in the path and returns its operation. The body names the site: confirm must equal the site's name. The site stops serving once the operation tombstones it, and its address is held for 90 days. Backups are kept. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation. Answers 409 while another change to the site is running.

get.summary: Read the state of the first admin password
get.description: Says whether the first admin password can still be revealed, without revealing it. It needs a signed-in session, so an API key is refused, and the answer is never cached. A site of another organisation is not found.

post.description: Returns the admin password the new site generated, once. It needs a signed-in session, so an API key is refused. A second call, an expired password and a site of another organisation are all not found. Do not send an Idempotency-Key header: a replayed answer would store the password.

get.summary: Read the health of a site
get.description: Reads the site live through its own hostname and returns its health tree, whether it answers, and the readiness checks. The answer is kept for 15 seconds per site. A site that does not answer is reported as not responding, not as an error. A site of another organisation is not found.

post.summary: Update a site to the current release
post.description: Starts an update of the site in the path to the platform's current release and returns its operation. The platform picks the target; the request has no body. The site keeps serving while the engine uploads the new release, checks the site, and puts the old release back if the check fails. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation. Answers 409 when the site already runs the current release or another change to it is running, and 422 when the site is not live.

get.description: Returns one site of your organisation. A site still being created is not found.

get.summary: List the operations of a site
get.description: Lists the operations of one site, newest first, in pages of up to 100.
Lists the site templates with their category, whether they are free and whether they can be used now. Disabled templates carry a Coming Soon label.

session.name: __Host-drupflare_session
session.description: The session cookie set at sign-in.

apiKey.description: An API key that starts with dfk_. Session-only actions refuse keys.

ContractHeader.name: Drupflare-Contract
ContractHeader.description: The contract versions the client understands, as common=<min>-<max>. A server that cannot serve the range answers 426.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Repeat a write safely. The same key with the same request returns the first result.

RequestId.description: The id of this request. Quote it when you contact support.

Contract.description: The contract versions this server supports, as common=<min>-<max>.

RateLimitLimit.description: Requests allowed in the current window.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

RateLimitReset.description: Seconds until the window frees a slot.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before the next request.

BadRequest.description: The request is invalid. details.issues lists each field path.

Unauthenticated.description: The request has no valid session or API key.

Forbidden.description: The caller may not do this.

Unprocessable.description: The Idempotency-Key was used for a different request.

ContractUnsupported.description: The server does not support the requested contract range. details.supported names the range it does.

InternalError.description: The server failed. Quote the requestId when you report it.
